ἀνόμους. ἅμα δὲ τηρεῖ καὶ τὸ ἀκριβὲς αὐτοῦ· Ἐγενόμην τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὡς Ἰουδαῖος·
οὐκ εἶπεν ἐνθάδε, Μὴ ὢν Ἰουδαῖος. Ἰουδαῖος γὰρ ἦν ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ, οὐκέτι ἐν τῷ
φανερῷ.καὶ πάλιν Τοῖς ὑπὸ νόμον ὡς ὑπὸ νόμον, μὴ ὢν αὐτὸς ὑπὸ νόμον·
ἀναγκαίως ἐνθάδε ἔθηκεν τὸ Μὴ ὢν ὑπὸ νόμον· Χρι τὸ γὰρ ἡμᾶ ἐξηγόρα εν ἐκ τῆ
κατάρα τοῦ νόμου, γενόμενο ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν κατάρα· ὡσανεὶ ἔλεγεν, Μὴ ὢν Σαμαρεύς.
Τοῖς δὲ ἀνόμοις ὡς ἄνομος, μὴ ὢν ἄνομος θεῷ. ἀλλ' ὑπολήψεταί μέ τις ἀπο στάτην
τοῦ νόμου γεγονέναι καὶ ἄνομον τῷ θεῷ· φημὶ δὲ ὅτι εἰ καὶ μὴ τηρῶ τὸν νόμον κατὰ
τὸ ῥητὸν οὐκ εἰμὶ ἄνομος τοῦ θεοῦ ἀλλ' ἔννομός εἰμι τοῦ Χριστοῦ τηρῶν τὴν
πολιτείαν τὴν κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, ἵνα κερδήσω τοὺς ἀνόμους. Ἐγενόμην τοῖς
ἀσθενέσιν ὡς ἀσθενής· οὐκ εἶπεν ἐνθάδε Μὴ ὢν αὐτὸς ἀσθε νής· ἀλαζονικὸν γὰρ ἦν,
ὑπερήφανον ἦν, οὐκ ἦν κατὰ τὸν ἀπόστολον εἰπεῖν Οὐκ ὢν αὐτὸς ἀσθενής, τὸν ἀπὸ
κυρίου ἀκούσαντα ὅτι ἡ δύναμί μου ἐν ἀ θενείᾳ τελειοῦται καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἐν
ἀ θενείαι καυχώμενον. πῶς δὲ Τοῖς ἀσθενέσιν ἀσθενής; ὅτε ἐπιτρέπει τοὺς
πυρουμένους γαμεῖν, ὅτε συμπάσχει ταῖς ἀπο βαλούσαις ἄνδρας, ὅτε φησὶ ∆ιὰ δὲ τὰ
πορνεία ἕκα το τὴν ἑαυτοῦ γυναῖκα ἐχέτω καὶ ἑκά τη τὸν ἴδιον ἄνδρα ἐχέτω καὶ τὰ
λοιπά. ἐν τούτοις ἐγένετο τοῖς ἀσθε νέσιν ἀσθενής, ἵνα τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς κερδήσῃ. Εἶτα
μετὰ ταῦτα λέγει Τοῖς πᾶσι γέγονα τὰ πάντα ἵνα πάντας ἢ τινὰς σώσω. Ὃν ἐὰν
λάβῃς ἄνθρωπον, ἓν τῶν πέντε ἐστίν· ἢ γὰρ Ἰουδαῖός ἐστιν, ἢ ὑπὸ νόμον, ἢ ἄνομος,
ἢ ἀσθενής, ἢ πάντα ἐστίν. ὁ τέλειος πάντα ἐστίν· τοῖς οὖν πᾶσι, τοῦτ' ἐστὶ τοῖς
τελείοις, γέγονα τέλειος, ἵνα πάντας κερδήσω. Σοφίαν γάρ φησι λαλοῦμεν ἐν τοῖ
τελείοι καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. οὗτος δύναται εἰπεῖν Ἕλλη ί τε καὶ βαρβάροι , οφοῖ τε καὶ
ἀνοήτοι ὀφειλέτη εἰμί.
[Ὠριγένους] Μόνος ὁ τέλειος δύναται εἰπεῖν τὴν τοῦ
τελείου ἀποστόλου ἐν κυρίῳ φωνὴν τὴν Πάντα ποιῶ διὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον. ὁ γὰρ
ἁμαρτάνων οὐ δύναται τοῦτο εἰπεῖν. εἰ δὲ ὁ πάντα ποιῶν διὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον
κοινωνός ἐστι τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, ὁ ποιῶν δὲ τὴν πορνείαν κοινωνός ἐστι τῆς πορνείας
τοῦ πνεύματος, ὁμοίως καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν ἄλλων παθῶν. ἕκαστος οὖν κοινωνὸς ἐκείνῳ ᾧ
ἐκοινώνησεν γίνεται. ἀλλ' ἐρεῖ τις τῶν ἀκουόντων Ὁ βίος μου μικτός ἐστιν· οὔτε
πάντα ποιῶ διὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, οὔτε πάντα ποιῶ διὰ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν καὶ τὴν ἡδονήν.
πρὸς τοῦτο φήσομεν Ταῦτα ὁ θεὸς τὰ κρίματα ἔχει· κατὰ τὰ κρίματα τὰ πολλὰ
ποικίλα ἀποδίδωσι. 44 ix 24 [Οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ ἐν σταδίῳ τρέχοντες, πάντες μὲν

pass_a_gloss: Fragment continues mid phrase on the lawless. Paul simultaneously keeps precision of speech. Lemma ‘I became to the Jews as a Jew’: he does not add ‘not being a Jew,’ because he remained Jew in the hidden sense, no longer in the open sense. Next lemma: ‘to those under law as under law, not myself under law’—the denial ‘not under law’ is required here, since Christ bought us out from the curse of the law by becoming curse for us; the force is like saying he is not a Samaritan. Then ‘to the lawless as lawless, not being lawless toward God.’ An objector will think Paul has become apostate from the law and lawless to God. Answer: even if he does not keep the law by the letter, he is not lawless of God but in law of Christ, observing the gospel way of life, so that he may gain the lawless. Next: ‘I became to the weak as weak.’ He refuses to say ‘not myself weak,’ because that would be boastful and proud and unfit for an apostle who heard ‘my power is completed in weakness’ and therefore boasts in weaknesses. How weak to the weak? By allowing those on fire with desire to marry; by sharing the pain of women who lost husbands; by the counsel that each have own wife and each own husband because of porneias, and similar concessions. In these acts he became weak to win the weak. Afterward: ‘I have become all things to all so as to save all or some.’ Take any human: he falls into one of five classes—Jew, under law, lawless, weak, or ‘all.’ The perfect person is ‘all’; therefore to all (meaning the perfect) he became perfect to win all. He also says we speak wisdom among the perfect, and so on. Such a person can claim debtorship to Greeks and barbarians, to wise and unwise. Origen: only the perfect may speak the perfect apostle’s voice in the Lord, ‘I do everything because of the gospel.’ A sinner cannot say that. The one who does all for the gospel shares the gospel; the one who does porneia shares the porneia of the spirit; same for other passions. Each becomes a sharer of that with which he shared. Hearer’s objection: my life is mixed—neither all for gospel nor all for sin and pleasure. Reply: God holds these judgments and pays back by his many varied judgments. Fragment 44 on the stadium race: do all of us run and only one take the prize while others perish? Paul said one prize taker among many runners. But all who are being saved are one and one body, because we partake one bread and are Christ’s body; therefore all the saved are that one prize taker. Stadium runners are all who live by a dogma: heretics living by dogma, perhaps Jews, and Greek philosophers living by Greek dogma; the church also runs; yet one takes the prize—the one man toward the perfect measure of Christ’s fullness. Still every divine judgment must appear over all stadium runners so someone takes firsts and each gets what fits his worth. Fragment 45 on God not well pleased with most who fell in the wilderness: the apostle’s aim is to show that receiving God’s gift does not by itself save the receiver; after receiving, one must remain and become worthy of the gift. The open cut breaks here mid sentence.
pass_b_english: —the lawless. At the same time he keeps his own exactness. “I became to the Jews as a Jew”: he did not say here, “not being a Jew.” For he was a Jew in secret, no longer in the open. And again: “to those under law as under law, though not myself under law”—here he had to put “not myself under law,” for [[Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law >> Bible:Galatians 3:13]], becoming a curse for us; as if he said, “not being a Samaritan.” “To the lawless as lawless, not being lawless toward God.” Someone will suppose I have become an apostate from the law and lawless toward God; I say that even if I do not keep the law according to the letter, I am not lawless toward God but under Christ’s law, keeping the polity according to the gospel, that I may win the lawless.

“I became to the weak as weak”: he did not say here “not myself being weak.” For it would have been boastful and arrogant, and not according to the apostle, to say “not myself being weak,” when he had heard from the Lord that [[my power is perfected in weakness >> Bible:2 Corinthians 12:9]] and for that reason boasts in weaknesses. How then was he weak to the weak? When he permits those who burn to marry; when he sympathizes with women who have lost husbands; when he says, [[because of porneias let each man have his own wife and each woman her own husband >> Bible:1 Corinthians 7:2]], and the rest. In these he became weak to the weak, that he might win the weak. Then after this he says, “I have become all things to all, that I may save all or some.” Whichever person you take, he is one of the five: either Jew, or under law, or lawless, or weak, or “all.” The perfect is all; so to all—that is, to the perfect—I have become perfect, that I may win all. For he says, [[we speak wisdom among the perfect >> Bible:1 Corinthians 2:6]], and what follows. This one can say, “I am a debtor both to Greeks and barbarians, both to wise and to unwise.”

[Origen:] Only the perfect can utter the perfect apostle’s word in the Lord: “I do all things for the sake of the gospel.” The one who sins cannot say this. If the one who does all for the gospel is a partner of the gospel, the one who commits porneia is a partner of the porneia of the spirit—and likewise with the other passions. Each becomes partner of that with which he shared. But someone among the hearers will say, “My life is mixed: I do not do all for the gospel, nor all for sin and pleasure.” To this we will say: God has these judgments; according to his many and varied judgments he repays.

44 on [[1 Corinthians 9:24 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 9:24]]: “Do you not know that those who run in a stadium all run, but one receives the prize? So run that you may obtain.” [Origen:] Then do we all run and one receives the prize, and the rest perish? For he said one receives the prize while many run. All who are being saved are one and one body; for if we all share one bread and the same bread, we are all Christ’s body. So all the saved are the one who receives the prize. In the stadium, then, all run who order their life by a doctrine—those from the heresies who live by a doctrine, and perhaps Jews, and those who live by Greek doctrines while philosophizing. These are all who run in the stadium; the church also runs; but one receives the prize—the one man of whom the apostle says, [[until we all attain to a perfect man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ >> Bible:Ephesians 4:13]]. Yet every judgment of God must be found concerning all who run in the stadium, so that one may take first place and then each according to his worth.

45 on [[1 Corinthians 10:5 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 10:5]]: “But with most of them God was not well pleased, for they were struck down in the wilderness.” [Origen:] The apostle wants to show us that it is not merely obtaining a gift of God that saves the one who obtained it, but that after obtaining the gift one must remain, having become worthy of it.
